## Context / Problem

Making OperationSnapshot authoritative for LLM operations (gaudy-working-mantaray) migrates `LLMConfig.from_env` call sites and threads a snapshot-derived projection through the gate/workflow entry points. `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (799 LOC) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (796 LOC) are within a few lines of the hard 800-LOC module-size cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so that threading would breach the CI module-size gate on first edit.

Create headroom FIRST via behavior-preserving extraction along existing call-graph seams. This story adds no snapshot-threading logic; it only relocates existing clusters.

## Approach

- `llm/config.py`: move `_env_truthy`, `_read_llm_file_table`, `_llm_str_source`, `_llm_str`, `_llm_int`, `_llm_float`, `_llm_drain_mode` into a new sibling `llm/config_readers.py`. `config.py` re-imports all of them (`from .config_readers import (...)  # noqa: F401`) at module top, mirroring the existing `gate_context` re-export pattern (config.py L41-47). `LLMConfig.from_env` (the sole caller) is NOT moved, so its bare-name lookups resolve through `config.py`'s own namespace — this is what keeps the ~15 existing `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` seams live. `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`'s direct `_read_llm_file_table` import keeps working via the re-export.
- `llm/plan_review/__init__.py`: move ONLY the five pure leaves — `_apply_floor_to_verdict`, `_score_floor_novelty`, `_apply_completion_floor_to_verdict`, `_classify_completion`, `_group_blocking_fix_units` — into a new sibling `llm/plan_review/floors.py`, re-imported (`from .floors import (...)  # noqa: F401`). `_maybe_apply_rising_floor` and `_maybe_apply_completion_floor` STAY in `__init__.py`: they are the entry points `_run_plan_review` calls, and their internal bare-name calls into the five moved leaves must keep resolving through `__init__.py`'s namespace so `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_score_floor_novelty"/"_classify_completion", ...)` (test_plan_review_rising_floor.py, test_completion_floor.py) keeps intercepting. `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_maybe_apply_rising_floor"/"_maybe_apply_completion_floor"/"_group_blocking_fix_units", ...)` (test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py) is unaffected either way since its caller `_run_plan_review` also stays put.
- **`_verifier_cfg`** stays in `__init__.py` (used elsewhere there too). The two moved leaves that call it (`_score_floor_novelty`, `_classify_completion`) reach it via a **lazy in-function import** (`from rebar.llm.plan_review import _verifier_cfg`), not a module-top-level import — `__init__.py` already does `from .floors import (...)` at its own top, so a reverse top-level import in `floors.py` would cycle. By call time the package is fully initialized, so the lazy import is safe; this mirrors the lazy-import style these two functions already use for `rebar.llm.runner`/`review_kernel.verify`/`passes`.

`LLMConfig`, `review_plan`, and public plan_review imports keep working unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/` — new sibling modules (`config_readers.py`, `plan_review/floors.py`); import updates only. Does NOT touch `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (owned by hurt-antigorite-genet).
- `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/` — import-path updates only, EXCEPT two consumers that pin a physical path/text and must be repointed:
  - `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` AST-parses `config.py`'s source TEXT by path (`_CONFIG_PY`) to enumerate `_llm_*` helpers; repoint `_CONFIG_PY` to `config_readers.py` (or also parse it) so the moved names keep being found.
  - `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`'s `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` hard-codes `'llm/plan_review/__init__.py::_score_floor_novelty'`; update to `'llm/plan_review/floors.py::_score_floor_novelty'`.

## Testing

Existing llm/plan-review suites (`tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/`) pass unchanged — every `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` site and every `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "<floor-helper>", ...)` site (rising-floor, completion-floor, completion-floor-e2e, blocking-fix-unit-grouping, sidecar-heldout tests) keeps intercepting the same call. The two path-pinning consumers above are updated and continue to pass. Module-size gate, complexity ratchet, lint, typecheck pass. No new CI-provider/network/Docker dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `config.py` and `plan_review/__init__.py` are each <= 700 LOC via extraction into `config_readers.py` / `plan_review/floors.py` only.
- [x] No new module < 100 LOC; no mechanical split.
- [x] Every existing monkeypatch seam on a moved helper via its ORIGINAL module keeps intercepting the same call site.
- [x] `test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py`'s `_CONFIG_PY` control and `test_subcall_class_selection.py`'s `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` entry are updated to the new locations and pass.
- [x] `floors.py` reaches `_verifier_cfg` via a lazy in-function import; no top-level circular import with `__init__.py`.
- [x] Behavior unchanged across `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/`.
- [x] `model_classes.py`'s `_read_llm_file_table` import keeps working unchanged.
- [x] `llm/runner.py` untouched.
- [x] Module-size gate, complexity ratchet, lint, typecheck all pass.
